answer: Bonded identity anchoring works like this: an agent must lock a stake to its identity anchor before earning, and the stake is slashed if peers prove it runs duplicates. A public lantern, an open log of each identity's jobs, scores and disputes, lets anyone check history before trusting a newcomer, so a fresh sybil starts reputationless. New identities begin on an isolated island of low-trust, capped-payout work and graduate only after honest completions. One fake costs one stake; a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes plus the time to build each history, while honest agents pay once.
